ian-finops: Heads up  Mid-market customer "GeoFleet" has split billing: billing address in Germany but seats used by drivers across EU (IE/FR). Invoices auto-charged DE VAT 19% but customer says some seats should be zero-rated or charged at local VAT. How do we handle split-country usage?

clara-tax: Split-supply is messy. For SaaS, place of supply for B2B is usually the customer's business location (billing VAT ID) -> reverse charge if EU B2B and VAT ID valid. For B2C or when seats are supplied to consumers in different member states, VAT is due at customer consumption location and OSS may apply.

ian-finops: GeoFleet provided a German VAT ID and some driver emails show Ireland/France local addresses. They want a per-seat breakdown and reissue for the seats that should be taxed locally.

sophie-cs: Customer uploaded list of seats with country codes and asked to split invoice lines accordingly. They prefer one consolidated invoice but need correct VAT treatment per seat.

clara-tax: Options: 1) If GeoFleet is a B2B (has valid DE VAT ID) and purchases for business purposes, the entire supply can be reverse-charged to DE under Article 196, even if seats are used elsewhere. Need VIES validation screenshot and a customer attestation that seats are for business use. 2) If any seats are for end-consumers, those should be taxed where the consumer is located; we'd need to collect VAT per-seat (OSS) or have partner handle local VAT. 3) If customer wants per-seat local VAT, we can reissue invoices with line-level place-of-supply but need to capture supporting evidence and adjust accounting entries.

ian-finops: They want option 3. How invasive is that?

clara-tax: It requires: - Per-seat country evidence (IP logs, seat assignment docs) - Customer attestation of which seats are company employees vs public consumers - Updated billing metadata to support line-level VAT, and likely engineering work. Also we must ensure compliance with OSS thresholds and local registrations if we act as seller in multiple EU countries.

acct-pay: For reissue path: we'll need original invoice number INV-2027-4521, the per-seat mapping file, validated VAT IDs (if B2B reverse-charge seats exist), and tax approval. Create FIN-6622.

oss-bot: Note: If Redwood chooses OSS simplification for B2C seats, we must enable OSS flag in merchant settings and submit quarterly OSS returns. Ticket: OSS-setup required.

marta-legal: Also check contract language: who is supplier of record and whether customer accepts to bear VAT liabilities for seats used abroad. Need signed amendment if we change billing logic.

ian-finops: Practical ask: can we do a one-off reissue now to satisfy GeoFleet and then evaluate product change later?

clara-tax: Yes, one-off reissue is possible with sufficient evidence. Steps: 1) Get seat mapping CSV and customer attestation. 2) Tax to review and map lines to VAT rates. 3) AP to issue credit note for INV-2027-4521 and reissue invoices: Invoice A (B2B reverse-charge for corporate seats) + Invoice B (local VAT lines for consumer seats). 4) Attach VIES validation/screen captures and attestation to FIN-6622.

ian-finops: I'll ask customer for seat CSV and attestation now. Also, can we avoid gross-up asks? They asked if Redwood can absorb local VAT for a promo-run.

clara-tax: Absorbing VAT = commercial concession. If agreed, Redwood pays VAT to tax authorities and treats it as an expense; need finance signoff. Tax prefers to keep VAT collection faithful to place-of-supply rules and not absorb unless pre-approved.

acct-pay: Created FIN-6622 and set status "awaiting docs". Please upload seat CSV and attestation to the ticket.

ian-finops: Customer uploaded seat CSV and a signed attestation stating "All seats are used by GeoFleet employees for business purposes except seats S23-S30 which are contractor drivers and should be taxed locally." CSV attached.

clara-tax: Received. Running through mapping now. VIES validated DE VAT ID (screenshot attached). For the contractor seats, we need country evidence per seat; IP logs or contract IDs suffice. If validated, we'll proceed with credit + two reissued invoices.

sophie-cs: I'll request the IP logs and driver contracts and upload to FIN-6622.

marta-legal: Once reissue confirmed, I'll draft a short amendment to the billing terms to cover future split-billing handling.

acct-pay: Noted. We'll wait for tax signoff then process credit note and reissues. Ticket FIN-6622 will track.

ian-finops: Thanks everyone. Customer asked for ETA: can we turn around in 5 business days?

clara-tax: Likely yes if we get all evidence within 48 hours. We'll aim for 5 business days.

acct-pay: Closing when FIN-6622 moves to 'ready to reissue'.
